title: Contractive linear extension from a dense subspace
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $k$ be a normed field [def-weil-field], meaning a field with a multiplicative absolute value satisfying the triangle inequality and defining the metric $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. Let $E$ and $F$ be normed $k$-vector spaces: their norms vanish exactly at zero, satisfy the triangle inequality and $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, and define their metric topologies. Assume that $F$ is complete, meaning every Cauchy sequence converges. Let $D\subseteq E$ be a $k$-linear subspace dense for the norm topology, with its induced norm. Every $k$-linear map $u:D\to F$ satisfying $\|u(x)\|\leq\|x\|$ for all $x\in D$ has a unique continuous $k$-linear extension $\widetilde u:E\to F$. This extension satisfies $\widetilde u(x)=u(x)$ for $x\in D$ and $\|\widetilde u(x)\|\leq\|x\|$ for all $x\in E$. No completeness of $E$ or $D$ is required.
